source.title: Train Large, Then Compress: Rethinking Model Size for Efficient Training and Inference of Transformers
source.authors: Zhuohan Li; Eric Wallace; Sheng Shen; Kevin Lin; K. Keutzer; D. Klein; Joseph E. Gonzalez

record.tranche_reason: The study reports results that qualify how model size relates to validation performance: returns diminish for the largest models, and the useful model size depends on dataset size. It does not fit the scaling laws or compute-optimal allocation described in most claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on model-size sweeps, dataset-size subsampling, and downstream fine-tuning, so these are recorded. Its references to scaling laws and results from other papers are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The paper sweeps RoBERTa width and depth under its own method, not a scaling-law fit. It reports that MLM perplexity depends mainly on parameter count rather than shape (V4). It also reports that models stopped at matched pretraining perplexity reach comparable downstream accuracy (V6). It fits no power law, extrapolation or compute-optimal frontier.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that wider and deeper Transformers converge faster in steps and in wall-clock time, and are more robust to quantization and pruning. The best strategy under resource limits is therefore to train large, stop early, then heavily compress. They add that MLM convergence depends mainly on parameter count rather than shape, that returns diminish for the largest models, and that the optimal size depends on dataset size.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares Transformer model sizes using validation perplexity, BLEU, wall-clock time, and downstream accuracy; it does not use the original scaling-law fitting or extrapolation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset size changes the outcome: on 5% data the largest models do not improve training time over smaller ones, and on 1% data larger models can have worse perplexity due to overfitting. Returns also diminish at the largest tested model sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed wall-clock time or FLOPs, larger RoBERTa and MT models reach lower perplexity or higher BLEU than smaller ones. Returns diminish at the largest sizes, partly because of hardware compute-boundness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At a fixed compute budget, larger models trained for fewer steps outperform smaller converged models, up to hardware-dependent limits (qualitative compute-optimal direction).

fits_no_version.finding: With 5% data the largest models give no speed gain, and with 1% data larger models overfit and reach worse perplexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of model size depends on dataset size when data is the bottleneck.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119, 2020
record.problems: The study does not fit power laws or report their uncertainty. Several learning-curve outcomes are presented in figures without tabulated numerical values. Training-time measurements use a single V100 GPU setup and the authors note that runtime varies by hardware.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small fits to larger runs.
Only a qualitative result: larger models trained for fewer steps win at fixed wall-clock time or FLOPs. No loss-minimising frontier or exponents are given.
Machine translation is trained and scored by BLEU curves, with no power-law form tested. No other modality.
Only six RoBERTa configurations over a narrow perplexity range (3.9–4.3) on two tasks. No fitted downstream-versus-scale relation.
No exponents are fitted and no fitting choices are compared.

missing.what: MLM validation perplexity depends weakly on depth versus width; parameter count determines convergence (V4).
missing.locator: Section 3, 'Increase Model Width and Sometimes Depth'; Figures 3, 4 and 10

missing.what: FLOPs-based learning curves: bigger models achieve lower perplexity at the same FLOPs.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V7 links were wrong. The paper fits no laws, so rows r1–r4 do not bear on fit-dependence; they are moved to fits_no_version. The V4 evidence was missed and should be added as a row. Rows r11 and r14 are duplicates. The study cites Kaplan et al. 2020 as concurrent work reaching similar conclusions.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit of held-out pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from small runs to substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute search for loss-minimising parameter and token allocations, and no fitted growth trends.
The study varies width and depth but does not report matched-parameter-count comparisons of architecture shapes.
The experiments concern NLP pretraining and machine translation; no other modality or training regime is tested.
Downstream evaluation is limited to MNLI and SST-2 at approximately matched pretraining perplexity; no general predictive relationship across tasks is fitted.
The study does not estimate scaling exponents, compare fitting methods, or directly test parameter-counting choices or training-schedule choices.

rows.subject: RoBERTa models of different sizes
rows.operation_detail: Compared validation MLM perplexity against wall-clock training time across model sizes.
rows.measure: Validation MLM perplexity as a function of wall-clock time
rows.value: figure only; the text says the largest models stop improving convergence with respect to wall-clock time
rows.note: The paper attributes diminishing returns to decreasing per-step convergence gains and increasing computational overhead.
rows.check: The measure is perplexity against wall-clock time on specific hardware. The diminishing returns are attributed partly to hardware becoming compute-bound. This is not loss against parameters, tokens or FLOPs, and no fit is made, so it does not bear on V7's claim about fitted exponents. Moved to fits_no_version.

conditions.value: validation MLM perplexity and training time

rows.measure: Validation MLM perplexity and training time across model sizes
rows.value: The largest models do not improve on the training time of smaller models; for example, 12-layer RoBERTa trains just as fast as 24-layer RoBERTa.
rows.note: The text reports an aggregate comparison across the plotted model-size sweep.
rows.check: This is the data-limited regime (5% of data), compared on wall-clock speed. V1 explicitly excludes cases where data is the bottleneck. No fit is made, so it does not bear on V7.

rows.subject: RoBERTa models (256H, 12L; 768H, 3L; 768H, 12L; 768H, 24L)
rows.operation_detail: Compared model-size learning curves after subsampling the pretraining data.
rows.measure: Validation MLM perplexity across model sizes
rows.value: The bigger models are worse in terms of perplexity due to overfitting.
rows.note: The text reports this as an aggregate outcome of the 1% data sweep.
rows.check: At 1% data, overfitting makes larger models worse. This is the data-bottleneck case the claim already excludes, and it is consistent with an L(N,D) form. It is not a reversal of any version, so state 'reversed' is wrong.

relationships.condition: RoBERTa MLM pretraining, depth {3–24} and width {256–1536} sweeps
relationships.reason: The text says validation perplexity 'weakly depends on the shape' and that parameter count is the key determiner (Section 3). No row records this; the verdict is based on the text and is figure-only.
relationships.display_finding: Validation perplexity depended weakly on shape, with parameter count the main determinant.

relationships.condition: Six RoBERTa sizes stopped at matched pretraining perplexity 3.9–4.3, fine-tuned on MNLI and SST-2
relationships.reason: Accuracies stay within about 1 point (MNLI 84.3–85.5, SST-2 92.6–93.8) at similar perplexity, consistent with loss predicting downstream performance. The range is narrow (r5–r16).
relationships.display_finding: At similar perplexity, MNLI accuracy stayed within 84.3–85.5 and SST-2 within 92.6–93.8, consistent with loss predicting performance over this narrow range.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
